name: French Polynesia

findings.controller: Alcatel-Lucent (submarine business now Alcatel Submarine Networks), turnkey supplier
findings.local_actor: Office des Postes et Télécommunications (OPT) de Polynésie française
findings.summary: OPT awarded Alcatel-Lucent a turnkey contract, about EUR 72.2m, for Honotua, a roughly 4,650 km Tahiti-Hawaii submarine cable plus a 305 km domestic inter-island link, with service targeted for 2010.
findings.analyst_inference: Controller convention follows GUF: French-state, French-company and EU controllers are 'third'; only Polynesian actors (OPT, Onati, TNT) are 'domestic'. Equipment rule makes the supplier Alcatel-Lucent (France; submarine arm now ASN, Nokia group) the controller. Tier 3 because the opened source documents the award only; a 2014 relayed Tahiti Infos item mentions the Honotua landing at Papenoo, implying it was built, but operation was not confirmed here. Pre-2020 and still_current not checked. EUR value not converted, so USD null.

findings.controller: Alcatel Submarine Networks (Nokia group), turnkey supplier
findings.local_actor: Office des Postes et Télécommunications (OPT) de Polynésie française
findings.summary: OPT signed a turnkey deal with Alcatel Submarine Networks in July 2017 for Natitua, a 2,500 km domestic cable linking Tahiti to Tuamotu and Marquesas islands; costing over XPF 6.5bn, it entered commercial service in December 2018.

sources.publisher: Direction générale de l'économie numérique, Polynésie française
Direction générale de l'économie numérique, Polynésie française

findings.analyst_inference: Controller convention follows GUF (French/EU = third; Polynesian = domestic). Equipment rule makes ASN the controller; the trade-press items likely relay one ASN release. Commissioning (tier 5) rests on the territorial DGEN pages, which list the 20 July 2017 OPT-ASN signing and December 2018 commissioning; they do not name the manufacturer themselves. XPF value not converted, so USD null. Current operation not separately checked, so still_current null.

findings.local_actor: Office des Postes et Télécommunications (OPT); subsidiary Onati assisted deployment
findings.builder: OMS Group (partnership with OPT); Alcatel Submarine Networks named as project partner
findings.financier: Government of French Polynesia investment subsidy to OPT
findings.summary: Natitua Sud extends OPT's domestic cable to Tubuai and Rurutu (Austral Islands); estimated at XPF 1.5bn with a territorial subsidy, it landed at Toahotu Bay, Tahiti, in April 2023, works due to end May 2023.

sources.publisher: Direction générale de l'économie numérique, Polynésie française

findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: the opened sources do not state who supplied the cable and terminal equipment. ASN is named only as a project partner and OMS Group as OPT's partner, so the equipment-rule controller is unconfirmed; if ASN supplied it, pole would be third. The two sources evidence different stages (2020 subsidy; 2023 landing). Completion and commissioning not confirmed in this run. XPF value not converted.

findings.local_actor: Manatua Consortium: OPT (French Polynesia), Avaroa Cables (Cook Islands), Telecom Niue, Samoa Submarine Cable Company
findings.financier: French State and Government of French Polynesia support; OPT share over EUR 20m
findings.summary: Manatua, about 3,600 km linking Samoa, Niue, the Cook Islands and Tahiti with a Bora Bora branch, was built by SubCom under a contract in force from November 2018 and declared ready for service July 2020; cost about EUR 41.9m.
findings.analyst_inference: Equipment rule makes US-headquartered SubCom the controller (pole us); OPT is a domestic consortium member. Outremers360 noted final negotiations were still needed before full operation at RFS. EUR values not converted, so USD null. Current operation not separately checked.

findings.summary: Vini began a phased non-standalone 5G rollout in Papeete and Faaa in August 2025, choosing Nokia as equipment and technical partner and committing over XPF 850m to 5G over five years.
findings.analyst_inference: Nokia (Finland) is third under the GUF convention. The press kit does not say whether Nokia supplies radio, core or both; the 5G layer is NSA on the existing 4G network, whose vendor is not named. Source tier S1 treats the operator's own launch press kit as a company notice; a reviewer could treat it as corporate communications (S4). Confidence kept low pending a second source. XPF not converted.

findings.builder: DRFortress (Hawaii), partner for build and colocation/cloud services
findings.summary: Tahiti's first data centre, at TNT's Papenoo site beside the Honotua landing, built with Hawaiian partner DRFortress for just under XPF 200m, was finished in August 2014 with first servers being installed.

sources.publisher: Tahiti Infos (relayed by DGEN, Polynésie française)
Direction générale de l'économie numérique, Polynésie française

findings.analyst_inference: Owner-operator rule: TNT (an OPT subsidiary per Outremers360) controls the building, so domestic; DRFortress is recorded as builder/partner. Tier 4 not 5: only completion and first installs are documented. Not corroborated because only the 2014 Tahiti Infos item evidences completion; the 2013 DGEN page is a Council of Ministers plan. Small, pre-2023 and pre-2020; current operation not confirmed. XPF not converted.
